title: Incident Evidence Enrichment Cookbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a lightweight, tactical cookbook for on-call engineers and first responders to rapidly enrich audit events and package evidence for SIEM export and downstream IR automation. Focus is RBAC V2-sensitive incidents (credential misuse, unexpected privilege changes, suspicious service tokens), but many steps apply to general auth/audit incidents.

When to use this doc:
- Pager/alert triggered by RBAC anomalies, policy drift, or spike in permission-grant events
- Suspicious login or token usage with minimal context in the raw audit event
- Follow-up when evidence automation (queue) returns incomplete artifacts

High-level goals (triage priorities):
1) Preserve a forensic snapshot (minimal blast radius)
2) Expand raw event with authoritative context (who, what, where, how long)
3) Push enriched artifact to SIEM with correct schema and retention tag
4) Record decisions and escalate if attack indicators rise

Quick TL;DR checklist (on-call condensed):
- Acknowledge alert in channel and mark incident id [INC-YYYYMMDD-XX]
- Snapshot: take API audit export (raw JSON), firewall/ingress logs for the timeframe, and process list from implicated host(s) if available
- Enrich: query identity service for actor metadata, resolve session/token lifetime, list granted roles and recent role-changes
- Label: add tags (rbac-v2, suspected-privilege-escalation, requires-SIEM-enrichment)
- Export: format and send to SIEM queue; submit short summary to #sec-oncall and link artifact

Detailed steps and recommended commands:
1) Incident identification and initial snapshot
- Create incident ID, create incident thread in #sec-oncall and PagerDuty entry. Timebox first-pass triage to 15 minutes.
- Export raw audit event(s): use the audit API v2: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_API_TOKEN" "https://audit.redwood.internal/v2/events?event_id=<id>" > raw-event.json
- If host involved, SSH with jump (do not reuse attacker creds): ssh -J bastion@jump redwood-host-01 -- sudo journalctl --since "-30m" | tail -n 500 > host-journal-snippet.txt

2) Identity enrichment (RBAC v2 context)
- Resolve actor principal: call identity service to map principal_id -> human/service account, linked GitHub/SSO id, last auth method. Example: http GET https://id.redwood.internal/principals/<principal_id> -> fields: display_name, email, team, service_owner, creation_ts
- Retrieve active role bindings for the principal at event_ts and at now. Use RBAC query: GET /rbac/v2/bindings?principal=<id>&at_ts=<ISO_TS>
- If role-change event: get change author, approved_by, request_id for self-service UI. Link to PR/approval flow.

3) Session & token context
- Token introspection: POST /auth/introspect {token} -> returns scope, issued_at, expires_at, origin_ip, client_id
- Correlate origin_ip with VPC logs/Cloud NAT to get subnet and region.
- Check for token replay: search last 24h for the token id in audit index. KQL (example for Kusto/Sentinel):
  EventType == "TokenUse" and TokenId == "<token-id>" | summarize count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h), SourceIP

4) Process and host enrichment (if applicable)
- Pull host process snapshot and network connections: sudo ss -tunap | egrep "<pid>|<port>" and ps -eo pid,ppid,cmd,user --sort=-%mem | head -n 40
- If containerized: capture container metadata (image sha, labels, runtime id) and container-runtime audit logs.

5) Evidence triage and packaging rules
- Minimum evidence bundle: raw-event.json, id-enrichment.txt, role-bindings.csv, token-introspect.json, host-snippet.txt (if host), SIEM-metadata.json (see mapping below), short incident notes.md
- Redaction: remove PII from host snippets unless necessary for investigation; mark redaction in metadata.
- Chain-of-custody header: include captured_at, captured_by (oncall name), storage_location (secure S3 path), retention_days

6) SIEM export mapping (required fields)
- SIEM field mapping example (send as a top-level flat map in SIEM-metadata.json):
  - incident_id: INC-YYYYMMDD-XX
  - event_id: <audit_event_id>
  - event_type: RBAC_BINDING_CHANGE | TOKEN_USE | AUTH_FAILURE
  - actor_id: <principal_id>
  - actor_display: <display_name>
  - actor_team: <team>
  - roles_at_event: role1;role2;role3
  - roles_before: roleA;roleB
  - source_ip: 1.2.3.4
  - source_asn:  AS12345 (if resolvable)
  - token_id: <token-id> (if present)
  - token_issued_at: 2025-01-02T15:03:00Z
  - token_expires_at: 2025-01-02T18:03:00Z
  - host: redwood-host-01
  - container_image_sha: sha256:abcd...
  - evidence_s3_path: s3://redwood-sec-evidence/INC-YYYYMMDD-XX/
  - retention_policy: 365d
  - rbacevidence_version: v1

7) Automated enrichment triggers (what to wire into the queue)
- If event_type == RBAC_BINDING_CHANGE and binding_scope == org-wide -> auto-enrich and page L2
- If token used from new geo or from TOR / high-risk ASN -> auto-enrich and attach Geolocation + ASN to SIEM artifact
- If service-account token used to create new role or create token -> escalate to L2 and lock token (if allowed)

8) Example queries (search snippets)
- Kusto/Sentinel: audit | where EventID == "RBAC_BINDING_CHANGE" and EventTime between (ago(1h) .. now()) | extend Principal = tostring(Details.principal) | sort by EventTime desc
- Splunk: index=audit event_type=rbac* principal_id=<id> | transaction token_id maxspan=1m | table _time, event_type, principal_id, token_id, src_ip

9) Communication templates (short)
- Pager/Slack initial: "[INC-{{id}}] RBAC anomaly detected for {{actor}} ({{actor_team}}). Triage started. Raw event captured and enrichment in progress. Paging L2. Evidence path: <link>."
- Update to stakeholders: include what was captured, risk level, containment actions taken, next steps, ETA for full write-up.

10) Containment play options (RBAC-specific)
- Temporary remove newly granted role (record exact binding removed and reason) OR 
- Add conditional policy that restricts token actions (if runtime supports) to limit blast radius
- If service token suspected, rotate token and create replacement with least privilege; schedule rollback window if client impact expected

11) Post-incident artifacts and handoff
- When incident transitions to postmortem, ensure evidence bundle is archived with access control lists set to sec-oncall and legal, retention set per incident severity
- Fill postmortem skeleton: summary, timeline, root-cause hypothesis, impact, remediation actions, prevention recommendations, verification plan, linked PRs/Jira

12) Short checklist for compliance auditors (quick checklist to attach to handoff):
- Raw audit event exports for all implicated event IDs
- RBAC binding snapshots (pre/post) with timestamps
- Token introspection results
- Evidence chain-of-custody metadata
- SIEM ingestion ticket / confirmation id

Operational notes / caveats:
- Avoid making lateral changes in prod while evidence is being collected. If containment is required, document the exact commands and timestamps used.
- On-call should not delete artifacts; mark as quarantined and move to secure bucket.
- Time-sync is important: use NTP-synced timestamps and include timezone (UTC recommended)

Retention and legal pointers:
- Default evidence retention is 365 days for incidents flagged as "security". For regulated incidents (customer-data exposure), escalate to legal and extend retention per guidance.
- Hash all evidence artifacts and include sha256 in SIEM-metadata.json for later verification.

Appendix A — Minimal incident timeline template (copy into incident notes.md):
- 00:00 Alert received: <source, summary>
- 00:03 First snapshot captured: raw-event.json, id-enrichment.txt
- 00:12 Enrichment complete: roles_before/after, token introspect
- 00:27 Containment action: removed binding X from principal Y (if taken)
- 01:05 SIEM export completed: upload_id=<id>
- 02:00 Handoff to L2/investigation team

Appendix B — Common gotchas and troubleshooting
- If RBAC query returns empty: check the query timestamp (bind changes are eventual-consistent for 2–10s, use at_ts +/- 30s window)
- If token introspection fails: token could be rotated; search for equivalent client_id and time-based correlation
- If SIEM rejects upload: verify schema fields, particularly event_time (should be ISO8601) and evidence_s3_path ACLs

Notes to reviewer / next steps:
- Add automation: a small lambda that takes audit webhook -> enriches via identity/rbac APIs -> writes SIEM-metadata and bundles to S3 and opens a Linear ticket automatically (SEC-412 is the tracking task).
- Provide mapping tests for SIEM ingestion; sample payloads should be stored under security-scripts/testdata/

- L2 escalation: Diego Martinez (pager)
- Product security lead: Lina Zhou (Slack DM)
